artifacts.summary: 7-phase plan rewriting all 34 source-store hook registrations to the $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR form, adding the missing merge-source counterpart, shipping an idempotent migration script for already-deployed repos, and demonstrating the guards blocking from a subdirectory CWD.

memory_candidates.content: When a defect lives in a DEPLOYED artifact whose source is install-once (copied only on first install, never overwritten by resync), a plan that only edits the source store can pass every gate while leaving every existing consumer repo broken. The correct phase decomposition is three-part, not one: (1) fix the source store, (2) ship an idempotent, --dry-run-capable migration script that repairs already-deployed copies in place (plus a de-duplication step, since an add-only merge will otherwise append the fixed entry alongside the surviving broken one), and (3) assert BOTH outcomes separately -- a fresh-deploy test for the source fix and a demonstration against a real pre-existing deploy for the migration. An acceptance criterion phrased as 'a fresh deploy produces X' is never sufficient on its own for an install-once surface.
